Thought: Nucleophilic addition reactions typically occur with carbonyl compounds (compounds containing C=O groups). The reactivity of carbonyl compounds toward nucleophilic addition depends on several factors:

1. Steric hindrance: Less steric hindrance around the carbonyl carbon makes it more accessible to nucleophiles.
2. Ring strain: Smaller rings have more strain, which can increase reactivity.
3. Electronic effects: Electron-withdrawing groups increase the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon.

Let's analyze each option:

A. Cyclopentanone: A five-membered ring ketone
B. Cyclopropanone: A three-membered ring ketone
C. Pentan-3-one: An acyclic ketone (also called diethyl ketone)

Cyclopropanone (B) has the most ring strain due to its small three-membered ring. This ring strain makes the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic and thus more reactive toward nucleophilic addition. The angle strain in the three-membered ring distorts the ideal geometry of the carbonyl group, making it more susceptible to attack.

Cyclopentanone (A) has less ring strain than cyclopropanone.

Pentan-3-one (C) is an acyclic ketone with no ring strain.

Therefore, the order of reactivity toward nucleophilic addition would be:
B. Cyclopropanone > A. Cyclopentanone > C. Pentan-3-one
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
